shortDescription: Apple NASDAQ:AAPL is considering the production of enterprise servers, utilizing its in-house chips, the M-series Ultra, and networking equipment from Nvidia NASDAQ:NVDA, according to The Information, citing people familiar with the situation.The Cupertino-based tech giant would sell the servers to…

children: is considering the production of enterprise servers, utilizing its in-house chips, the M-series Ultra, and networking equipment from Nvidia
, citing people familiar with the situation.

The Cupertino-based tech giant would sell the servers to AI developers, businesses and governments as it seeks to take advantage of the surging demand for compute, the report said. It would also herald Apple's return to the server market. From 2002 to 2011, Apple offered Xserve, powered by Intel
chips, but the product failed to find significant traction.
However, times are different now, as high-powered compute demand seems insatiable. In Apple's third-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings
, Mac sales surged 29% year over year to $10.3B, representing the largest percentage growth of any Apple category, including the iPhone and Services segments.

Apparently, AI labs and developers have stocked up on tens of thousands of its Mac mini and Mac Studio computers to help run their operations. A new server product could target this rapidly growing market.

However, the new server product would not be available until 2029, if Apple pursues it, the report said. It's also unknown if Apple would ultimately use Nvidia's NVLink Fusion product line, which includes switches, chiplets and software, in the servers. Still, new Apple CEO John Ternus backed the plan as long as a year ago, as it created an opportunity for Apple's custom silicon to enter the AI compute market.
Apple shares inched up 0.7% by later morning trading on Wednesday.

title: Apple considers building servers with in-house chips and Nvidia networking equipment: report
